en: The Prophecy of the Noble Śrīmahādevī [also known as the *Dvādaśadaṇḍakanāmāṣṭaśatavimalīkaraṇā*]. Om! Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sukhāvatī together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas— namely, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantabhadra,
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvabhayahara, and likewise by the bodhisattva Sarvamaṅgaladhārin.

with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who bears all marks of merit; with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who sustains the moon, the sun, and the three worlds; with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who sustains the auspiciousness of all heretics; and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta—by these and other such Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
Then indeed, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara approached the place where the Blessed One was;
having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
The Great Goddess Śrī also approached the Blessed One.

Having approached and circumambulated the feet of the Blessed One a hundred thousand times, and having bowed his head to all those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas dwelling in Sukhāvatī, he sat down to one side. Then the Blessed One— adorned by many hundreds of thousands of merits, surrounded by ten million Tathāgatas, and praised and extolled by all the Śakras,
Brahmās, and World-Protectors— seeing the Great Goddess Śrī, addressed the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara in a voice like that of Mahābrahmā:
O Avalokiteśvara, whatever king, royal official, monk, nun, layman, or laywoman, or any among the Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, or Śūdras,
shall maintain this hymn of one hundred and eight verses named *Vimalaprakhya* dedicated to the Great Goddess Śrī,
all fears and calamities of those beings within the realm of that Kṣatriya king shall be pacified.
There will be no fear from any thieves, rogues, humans, or non-humans; there will be an increase in all wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses;
and the goddess Śrī shall dwell in the palace of that Kṣatriya king.
Then those bodhisattva mahāsattvas spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! This speech is well-spoken."
"Those who shall uphold the names of the Great Goddess Śrī will also possess these qualities and benefits.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, where was the root of merit planted by the Great Goddess Śrī?"
The Blessed One said:
"The root of merit was planted by the Great Goddess Śrī in the presence of as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā.
Long ago, Avalokiteśvara, in a past age, in the world-system called Ratnasaṃbhavā, there was a Tathāgata named Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī."
He appeared in the world.
In his presence, the Great Queen Śrī planted roots of merit, as did many other Tathāgatas.
And these names of the Tathāgatas bring about the increase and perfection of the roots of merit of that Great Queen Śrī.

These [mantras], which have been proclaimed here by the Great Goddess Śrī and are ever-attendant upon her, remove all sins, destroy all defilements, purify all undertakings, attract and increase wealth and grain, cut through poverty,

and cause the propitiation and summoning of all gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; they pacify all calamities, misfortunes, distresses, and all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes.
They bring about the perfection of the six pāramitās.
Homage to the Tathāgata Śrīghana. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaidūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Gaṅgāsarvatīrthamukhamaṅgalaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Candanakusumatejonakṣatraprabhāsaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Dharmavikurvaṇadhvajavegaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Jyotiḥsaumyagandhāvabhāsaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Sattvāśayaśamanaśarīraśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Praṇidhānasāgarāvabhāsaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Suparikīrtitanāmadheyaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Asaṃkhyeyavīryasusaṃprasthitaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Aprameyasuvarṇottaprabhāsaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Sarvasvarāṅgarutanirghoṣaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Prajñāpradīpāsaṃkhyeyaprabhāketuśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Nārāyaṇavratasannāhasumeruśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Brahmaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Maheśvaraśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Candrasūryaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Gambhīradharmaprabhārājaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Gaganapradīpābhirāmaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Sūryaprabhāketuśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Gandhapradīpaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Sāgaragarbhasambhavaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Nirmitameghagarjanayaśaḥśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Sarvadharmaprabhāsavyūhaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Drumarājavivardhitaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnārciḥparvataśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Jñānārcisāgaraśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Mahāpraṇidhivegaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Mahāmeghaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Smṛtiketurājaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Indraketudhvajarājaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Sarvadhanadhānyākarṣaṇaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Saumyākarṣaṇaśrī;
homage to the Tathāgata Lakṣmyākarṣaṇaśrī.
These names of the Tathāgatas should be respectfully upheld and recited; in this way, that son of good family or daughter of good family will generate a much greater amount of merit.
And the noble Mahādevī was prophesied by the Tathāgatas:

"O noble Mahādevī, in a future time, in the world-system named Śrīmahāratnapratimaṇḍitā, you shall become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śrīmaṇiratnasambhava; and that world-system shall be adorned with various divine jewels."
And in that world-system, that very Tathāgata shall be the maker of light;
and those bodhisattvas in that buddha-field shall be self-luminous and possess immeasurable lifespans;
and from the sky, the sound of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha shall issue forth.
And all those bodhisattvas who shall be reborn in that buddha-field will be reborn upon the pericarps of lotuses.
In this regard, what is the hymn of praise known as the "One Hundred and Eight Verses in Twelve Stanzas," which resembles the stainless?
Listen, O Abhayāvalokiteśvara, to the names of the Great Goddess Śrī.
Namely: she who is consecrated by all the Tathāgatas, she who is consecrated by all the deities, the mother of all the Tathāgatas,

the mother of all the deities, the glory of all the Tathāgatas, the glory of all the Bodhisattvas, the glory of all the noble Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, the glory of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, the glory of Mahāsthānaprāpta, the glory facing all the deities, and the glory of all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.
The glory of all Vidyādharas, Vajrapāṇi, and Vajradharas; the glory of the four and five World-Protectors; the glory of the eight planets and twenty-eight lunar mansions.

Om! Sāvitrī, Dhātrī, Mātā, the glory of the four Vedas; Lakṣmī, Bhūtamātā, Jayā, Vijayā, Gaṅgā, the embodiment of all holy fords (tīrthas), the auspiciousness of all blessings, the glory that makes one stainless and pure, the destroyer of all sins, the remover of pride, the glory of the moon, the glory of the sun.

She is the glory of all planetary deities (*sarvagrahaśrī*), she who rides upon a lion (*siṃhavāhinī*), she who is covered by the openings of hundreds of thousands of millions of lotuses (*padmavivara*), she who is the Lotus (*padmā*), born from the Lotus (*padmasambhavā*), whose abode is the Lotus (*padmālayā*), who holds the Lotus (*padmadharā*), who possesses the Lotus (*padmāvatī*), she who wears a garland of rays from many jewels (*anekaratanāṃśumāla*), the Giver of Wealth (*dhanadā*), the White One (*śvetā*), the Great White One (*mahāśvetā*), she whose arms are white (*śvetabhujā*), the bearer of all auspiciousness (*sarvamaṅgaladhāriṇī*), her limbs accumulated with all merit (*sarvapuṇyopacitāṅgī*), the daughter of Dakṣa (*dākṣāyaṇī*), she who has hundreds of thousands of arms (*śatasahasrabhujā*), and she who has hundreds of thousands of eyes (*śatasahasranayanā*).

She who possesses a hundred thousand heads; she who wears a crown of various and diverse jewels; she of beautiful form; she of universal form; she of renown; she of great renown; she who is gentle; she who has many clouds; she of pure hair; she who is as lovely as the moon; she who is as radiant as the sun; she who is auspicious; she who performs auspicious deeds; she who faces all sentient beings; she who is the noble glory of flowers; she who is the sovereign of flowers.

She possesses the splendor of all Sumeru kings of mountains, the splendor of all rivers and streams, the splendor of all waters and oceans, the splendor of facing all sacred fords (*tīrtha*), and the splendor of all medicinal herbs, grasses, forest trees, wealth, and grain. She is the giver of gold, the giver of food and drink, radiant, light-making, pure of limb, and sovereign over all Tathāgatas. She is the splendor of the faces of all the hosts of gods, and the splendor of Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Vāsava.

She is the giver, the enjoyer, splendor, the radiant one, prosperity, abundance, growth, exaltation, the glory of Dharma, she who has Mādhava as her refuge, she whose abode is flowers, Anasūyā, she who takes refuge in human effort, she whose limbs are entirely pure, she whose hands hold auspiciousness, the destroyer of all misfortune, the glory that attracts all merit, the glory of the entire earth, the glory of all kings, the glory of all Vidyādhara kings, and the glory of all beings, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Pretas, Piśācas, Kumbhāṇḍas, and Mahoragas.

She whose splendor is restless with joy and fortune, whose glory is the purity of all sages, who is the glory of all, the supreme glory of the eldest of beings, and the supreme glory of all Kinnaras and Sūryas;
she who dwells in faultless places, who is beautiful, who brings happiness, the beloved of Kubera, and the glory of Dharmarāja:
Oṃ, look upon me! Deliver me! Liberate me from all sufferings! Bring before me the accumulation of all merits! Svāhā!
Oṃ, turn all the sacred fords, beginning with the Gaṅgā, toward this face; svāhā!
Oṃ, to Sāvitrī, svāhā!
To the bearer of all auspiciousness, svāhā!
Svāhā to the one whose form consists of the four Vedas, the constellations, the hosts of planets, and so forth; svāhā to Brahmā;
svāhā to Viṣṇu.
Svāhā to Rudra!
Svāhā to the one whose face is the universe!
Om Nigrigrini, accomplisher of all tasks, Sini Sini, I invoke you!
Svāhā to the goddess Śrī Vaiśravaṇa!
Svāhā to the one who attracts gold, wealth, and grain!
Svāhā to the one who attracts all merit!
Svāhā to the one who attracts the glorious deities!
Svāhā to the one who destroys all sins! Svāhā to the one who pacifies all misfortune!
Svāhā to her who is consecrated by all the Tathāgatas!
Svāhā to the glory that faces all the deities!
Svāhā to her who bestows long life, strength, and beauty!
Svāhā to her who holds all purifying and auspicious objects in her hands! Svāhā to her who rides upon a lion!
Svāhā to her who is born from a lotus!
*svāhā* to the one who destroys all malevolent rites and *kākhorda* spells!

These are the names of the Great Goddess, the Glorious Abhayāvalokiteśvarī; they destroy all defilements, bring about the destruction of all sins, attract all merit, pacify all misfortune, and attract all glory and good fortune.

Whoever shall recite these names of the Tathāgatas, having risen at dawn, being pure, and having offered flowers and incense to all the Buddhas and sandalwood incense to Śrī Mahādevī, shall attain all prosperity,
shall become a possessor of all happiness and mental well-being, and all the deities shall provide protection, defense, and guardianship.
"All his undertakings shall be successful.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Abhayāvalokiteśvara was uplifted in mind.
And that entire assembly, including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
